summary: Holmes County, MS tower the Register lists as a 90 ft Aermotor LS-40 with no build date; 1936 notices describe a CCC-built steel tower north of town, but the link is unconfirmed.

facts.design: Aermotor LS-40 tower, 90 ft per the Register (a July 1936 notice says 100 ft)
facts.status_note: Register describes the tower at its July 2023 site visit; no statement of current condition

access.note: Neither source describes public access; the Register describes a former county forester's site with a house and other buildings, so ask the Mississippi Forestry Commission before visiting

events.note: Steel fire tower built by the local CCC camp on the poor house property north of Lexington and completed by late August 1936, per Lexington Advertiser notices. Link to the Register tower not confirmed
Telephone line planned to take fire reports, and poles set to link the tower with other towers
Registered July 9, 2023 as US 1742, MS 59 after a July 2, 2023 site visit

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says 90 ft; the July 23, 1936 notice says 100 ft. The story reports both and does not choose one.
Name and county match between the 1936 notices and the Register entry, but no source says they describe the same structure. The story presents the link as unconfirmed.

notes_for_editor: Identity is the open question. The 1936 notices (quoted on Forest Lookouts from The Lexington Advertiser) describe a CCC-built steel tower on the poor house property north of Lexington. The Register entry has no build date and a 90 ft LS-40. Height conflict (90 vs 100 ft) is reported in the story, not resolved. A campground directory (refined-travel.com) calls a Forestry Department Fire Tower at 509 Lewis Rd, Lexington, but the listing is generic and unverified, so it is not cited. Original newspaper microfilm or MFC records would settle identity and height. No photos found. Access level is inferred from the absence of any access statement and the former county forester's site description.
